_exec_summary.SummaryText:
This is an executive summary of the policies, procedures, and activities for compliance with the EPA's Accidental Release Prevention Requirements - Risk Management Program pursuant to Title 40 Part 68 of the Code of Federal Regulations (40 CFR 68) for the QuestSpecialty facility at Brenham, TX.
The accidental release prevention and emergency response policies at the stationary source [40 CFR 68.155(a)]:
QuestSpecialty is strongly committed to employee, public and environmental safety. This commitment is demonstrated by our comprehensive accidental release prevention program that encompasses design, installation, operating procedures, maintenance, and employee training. Robust engineering controls are in place to prevent possible releases of regulated substances. The Brenham, TX facility is a non-responding facility for releases of RMP-listed chemicals, so the site utilizes an Emergency Action Plan.
The stationary source and regulated substances handled [40 CFR 68.155(b)]:
QuestSpecialty is a packager of aerosol and liquid cleaning products. LPG is used as a propellent in many of the aerosol products packaged. The facility consists of two 12,000-gallon storage tanks and one 6,580-gallon storage tank. These storage tanks are limited to a fill of 80% of total capacity. The facility complies with NFPA-58 requirements for LP-Gas storage and handling. QuestSpecialty's policy is to adhere to all applicable Federal, State and Local laws and guidelines, where applicable.
If an emergency were to occur, the Brenham Municipal Fire Department would be immediately
notified and requested to respond to the emergency.
QuestSpecialty has one (1) covered process (aerosol hydrocarbon flammable mixture of propane
and butane) at the Brenham Texas Facility that is classified as a Program 3 process and subject to the Program 3 prevention program requirements of the RMP rule. Program 3 prevention
program aligns with the requirements of the OSHA PSM standard.
The general accidental release p

revention program and chemical-specific prevention steps [40 CFR 68.155(c)]:
The facility has taken the necessary steps to comply with the accidental release prevention
requirements set out under 40 CFR Part 68. The following sections briefly describe the elements of the Release Prevention Program that are in place at the Brenham Facility.
Process Safety Information [40 CFR Part 68.65]
QuestSpecialty maintains a variety of technical documents that are used to ensure safe operation of the process. Process Safety Information includes information pertaining to hazards of the highly hazardous chemicals in the process, technology of the process, and equipment in the process.
Examples of Process Safety Information include, but are not limited to, safety data sheets, piping
and instrumentation diagrams, maximum intended inventory, pressure relief design/design basis, and safety systems. Process Safety Information is updated using the Management of Change (MOC) process. Process Safety Information is available electronically on QuestSpecialty internal server to ensure employee accessibility. This information informs employees of the hazards, safety precautions, and design related limits for the process.

Process Hazard Analysis [40 CFR Part 68.67]
Comprehensive analyses ensure that hazards associated with our processes are identified and controlled efficiently. The methodology used to carry out these analyses is HazOp . The studies are undertaken by a team of qualified personnel with expertise in engineering and process operations and are revalidated at a regular interval of 5 years. Any findings related to the hazard analysis are addressed in a timely manner.

Written Operating Procedures [40 CFR Part 68.69]
To ensure safe operations, QuestSpecialty maintains detailed written operating procedures. These procedures address various modes of operation such as initial startup, normal operations, temporary operations, emergency shutdown, emergency operations and normal shutdown.

The information is regularly reviewed and is readily accessible to operators involved in the processes.

Employee Training [40 CFR Part 68.71]
QuestSpecialty has a comprehensive training program in place to ensure that employees who are operating plant processes are competent in the applicable operating procedures. Refresher training is provided at least every three years and more frequently as needed.

Mechanical Integrity [40 CFR Part 68.73]
QuestSpecialty carries out documented maintenance checks on process equipment to ensure proper operations. Inspected process equipment include pressure vessels, storage tanks, piping systems, pressure relief and vent systems, emergency shutdown systems, controls, and pumps. Maintenance operations are carried out by qualified personnel with previous training in maintenance practices. Furthermore, these personnel are offered specialized training as needed. Any equipment deficiencies identified by the maintenance checks are corrected in a safe and timely manner.

Management of Change [MOC] [40 CFR Part 68.75]
Written procedures are in place at QuestSpecialty to manage changes in process chemicals, technology, equipment, and procedures. Facility operators or any other employee whose job tasks are affected by a modification in process conditions are promptly made aware of and offered training to deal with the modification(s).

Pre-Startup Safety Review [PSSR] [40 CFR Part 68.77]
Pre-start up safety reviews related to new processes and modifications to existing processes are conducted routinely at QuestSpecialty. These reviews are conducted to confirm that construction, equipment, operating, and maintenance procedures are suitable for safe startup prior to placing equipment into operation.

Compliance Audits [40 CFR Part 68.79]
QuestSpecialty conducts audits on a regular basis to determine whether the provisions set out under the US EPA RMP and OSHA PSM regulations are being implemented. These audits are conducted at least every 3

years and any corrective actions required as a result of the audits are undertaken in a prompt manner. The final resolution of each finding is documented, and the two most recent audit reports are kept on the internal server.

Incident Investigation [40 CFR Part 68.81]
QuestSpecialty promptly investigates any incident that has resulted in, or could reasonably result in a catastrophic release of a regulated substance. These investigations are undertaken to identify the situation leading to the incident as well as any corrective actions to prevent the release from reoccurring. All reports are retained for a minimum period of 5 years.

Employee Participation [40 CFR Part 68.83]
QuestSpecialty believes that Process Safety Management and accident prevention is a team effort. Employees are strongly encouraged to express their views concerning accident prevention issues and to recommend improvements. In addition, QuestSpecialty employees have access to all information created as part of the facility's implementation of the RMP and PSM rules, including information resulting from Process Hazard Analyses in particular.

Hot Work Permit [40 CFR Part 68.85]
QuestSpecialty has a hot work permit that requires issuance of a hot work permit for hot work operations conducted on or near the covered process. 

Contractor Safety Program [40 CFR Part 68.87] 
QuestSpecialty utilizes contract personnel to supplement maintenance work and also during planned shutdowns and construction activities. Prior to selecting a contractor, a thorough evaluation of the contractor's safety performance is carried out. QuestSpecialty has a strict policy of informing the contractors of known potential hazards associated with the contractor's work and the corresponding processes. Contractors are also informed of all the procedures for emergency response in the event of an accidental release of a regulated substance.
The five-year accident history [40 CFR 68.155(d)]:
The facilitys RMP process has had no acc

idents in the past five years.
The emergency response program [40 CFR 68.155(e)]:
QuestSpecialty has never had a significant release of hazardous substance defined by the RMP
Rule for the covered process. In the event of an emergency involving our LP-Gas system,
QuestSpecialty's policy is to notify the Brenham Municipal Fire Department and request that they help respond to the emergency. Members of the fire department have inspected the facility and are familiar with the operation. 
QuestSpecialty also has an Emergency Action Plan (EAP). The EAP describes requirements that must be followed in the event of a release involving our LP-Gas system or if an emergency arises during maintenance activities. Since QuestSpecialty employees will not respond to releases of regulated substances, the EAP defines the response organizations on call, emergency notification procedures (internal and external), facility evacuation, site communication and best practices to be used in the event an incident should occur. The EAP is reviewed and updated at least once per year to incorporate any facility changes.
Planned changes to improve safety [40 CFR 68.155(f)]:
While there are no planned changes to our safety program at this time , QuestSpecialty constantly reviews our safety program and institute revisions as appropriate to enhance safety and promote continuous improvement of our operations.
QuestSpecialty has prepared this report to inform the public about our activities at this facility. We believe that the safety controls we have in place, along with our commitment to continuous improvement, significantly reduce the likelihood of an incident affecting our employees or the surrounding community.
